_comment: Migration notes per Loom version, read by adopt.mjs. On an upgrade the installer prints every entry between the stamped version and this bundle's, so an adopter is told what changed and what they must do — rather than discovering it when a gate they have never heard of fails. `action_required` is the half that needs a human: a new template to fill, a new gate that only stays green once something is declared. Keep entries factual and short; the canon is the reference docs, not this file. A version with no adopter-visible change needs no entry.

versions.headline: The routine-change lane (HG-0013) — graduated autonomy behind an absolute control-plane floor
notes: A narrow, pre-named class of low-risk changes may auto-merge inside a second-line-owned, expiring envelope. Approval moves from per-change to per-envelope; it never disappears.
action_required: Fill docs/governance/routine-envelope.json (second-line owned) if you want the lane at all — leaving it unadopted simply means every change takes the human-merge lane.
Branch protection: mark `gates` required; do NOT mark `routine-qualified` required. Point the merge queue at `routine-qualified` alone.

versions.headline: The product-eval gate — a release scores its discovery success measures
notes: A release links its discovery hand-off and scores every D1 success measure against the shipping commit; a regression blocks.
action_required: Fill docs/governance/product-evals.json. The eval rig itself is yours to build — the gate checks that the result is sealed and bound to the shipping commit.

versions.headline: Token-spend telemetry
notes: docs/governance/token-ledger.json records per-iteration spend. It is a report and never a merge gate — cost is a signal for humans.

versions.headline: The policy compiler commands execution, and the Institutional BrainKit arrives
notes: Required gates are compiled from the change envelope's profiles rather than listed by hand, so a control cannot be talked off the route by editing CI.
institution/brainkit/ ships as adopt-pending templates; the installer never invents or approves institutional content.
action_required: If your institution owns a BrainKit, run the `brainkit-init` skill to draft one from approved sources, then have its owners approve it. Until then it stays dormant and no change pins it.

versions.headline: The release-evidence plane rebuilt on the artifact
notes: Source, artifact, evals and anchor must all bind to ONE digest. Release-evidence checks stopped masquerading as PR-source checks: the gate runner's lanes now cover build and deploy as well as pr, release and scheduled.
action_required: If you pinned CI to the `pr` lane only, add the `build`, `release` and `deploy` lane invocations — release-evidence gates no longer run on the PR lane.

versions.headline: Platform enforcement made real (WS2)
notes: A control graduates to platform-enforced only on a live observation that was bypass-tested, independently signed and fresh — a declared activation no longer counts.
Live control-plane config is reconciled against an approved baseline; drift suspends routine auto-merge.
action_required: Fill docs/governance/config-baseline.json with your approved control-plane configuration, and produce the live observation with `loom activate`.
docs/governance/routine-controller.yml is a reference auto-merge controller — it needs a bot identity separated from the coding agent before it means anything.

versions.headline: The approval-attestation contract, and runtime-neutral guardrails
notes: Human approval assertions are verified against identity-provider material kept separate from service keys.
The P6 identity map joins a signed subject to a registry identity — second-line owned, never written by a service.
guardrails/ declares what the runtime actually enforces, so the Loom never implies coverage a runtime lacks.
The data-risk register became mandatory-when-compiled: if a change's compiled plan requires it, a missing register fails D6 with no flag to turn it off.
action_required: Fill docs/governance/assertion-issuers.json and docs/governance/identity-map.json (both second-line owned).
Regulated adopters: mount a real data-risk register at docs/governance/data-risk-register/ — --require-register can now only tighten, never weaken.

versions.headline: Continuous-assurance cases, and the adoption state machine
notes: Signal-triggered assurance cases must be handled within an SLA, mapped, contained and decided by the second line.
`loom status` projects adoption as five stages with an unresolved-marker inventory.
action_required: Fill docs/governance/assurance-sla.json with the service-level expectations you can actually meet.

versions.headline: The BrainKit estate registry and the comprehension record
notes: No repository may run a revoked BrainKit release.
High-tier changes carry a human understanding record — the first mechanical push against comprehension debt.

versions.headline: The catalog closes over CI, the status board tells the truth, and upgrades stop destroying your edits
notes: Ten gates ran in CI with no control-catalog entry, so the risk-proportionate gate runner never selected them — including floor-only-check, which is what stops personal data crossing into the record. All are catalogued, and `ci-catalog-check` now fails the build if a gate is ever added to CI without one.
`loom status` gained a --run flag: the Mechanism column is the catalog's grade, the Passing column is what your repository actually does. They are not the same thing and no longer look the same.

The installer writes .loom/adoption.json and no longer overwrites files you have edited. A customised gate or hook is preserved and reported, with the new upstream version dropped beside it as a .loom-new sidecar.

The Factory Floor — the optional collaboration surface for people who never open a repository — is documented in the method canon for the first time (loom skill, references/factory-floor.md): the four planes, the three write classes, the freeze round trip, and an honest statement of what is and is not deployed. The machinery did not change; it was simply undocumented.
action_required: First upgrade onto a stamped adoption: files that differ from this bundle cannot be told apart from your edits, so ALL of them are preserved and reported as `unverifiable`. Reconcile the .loom-new sidecars, or re-run with --force if you know you never customised anything. Later upgrades know the difference and this will not recur.

versions.headline: Adoption tiers — you no longer have to adopt all of it at once
notes: `adopt.mjs --tier core|governed|full` stages the adoption. Core lands roughly eight files to fill instead of seventy-odd; governed adds the product-governance plane; full is everything and stays the default.
Every tier installs EVERY gate. Only what you must fill in is tiered — a gate whose input file is absent is silent, so deferred controls are already running and waiting rather than missing.
Core is the smallest adoption that is SAFE, not the smallest that installs: data-lifecycle.json and model-manifest.json fail closed when absent, so they stay in core.
A re-run with no --tier keeps the tier you already adopted; it never silently demotes. `loom version` reports it.
action_required: Nothing, if you are already adopted: an existing adoption has no recorded tier and is treated as full, which is what it is. Pass --tier explicitly only if you want to change it.

versions.headline: Three adversarial-checklist rows now meet the standard the playbook sets for them
notes: The pilot playbook defines CI-proven as "a negative bypass test in .github/workflows/validate.yml demonstrates the rejection". Three rows — stale model evaluation, fabricated evaluation artifact, vulnerable dependency — carried that grade with only positive gate runs behind them in CI.

The rejections were already unit-tested in scripts/*.test.mjs; what was missing was the adoption-level bypass test the playbook's own definition demands. All three now exist, and each row names its test the way every other proven row does.

versions.headline: The bundle is held to its own claims; CI runs from the catalog; a non-bank base profile
notes: New `self-claims-check` gate: prose may not cite a gate that does not exist, and a CI-proven claim must name the negative test that backs it or scope itself to the part it covers. Every defect the rc.18–rc.25 review found was this one shape — a claim and its evidence drifting apart — and each was fixed by hand after a human noticed. This makes the class mechanical.

The reference CI no longer carries an explicit gate list. It asks the control catalog what to run, per lane, via core/gate-runner.mjs — so the list-vs-runner divergence that let ten gates go uncatalogued cannot recur in a new form. Four gates the runner structurally cannot drive (Q1b's merge base, the per-directory D-gate loop, the token report, adoption-attest) stay as named steps, each `execute: false` in the catalog with a stated reason. Every run uploads gate-run-*.json: what ran, what skipped, and why.

New base profile `standard` — the warp and nothing more, for a team building with AI under ordinary engineering discipline. `regulated-bank` is now one of two bases rather than the floor of the system. A test asserts standard requires a SUBSET of regulated-bank at every tier, so choosing it can never hand you a control the stronger profile lacks.
template-parity-check finally has a regression suite, retiring the one catalog entry that had to admit it had none.
action_required: If you copied the old ci.yml, take the new one: it is behaviourally equivalent (same gates, same fail-closed results) but sourced from the catalog. Keep your own Q-gate additions.
Non-regulated adopters: name `standard` in a governed change's required_profiles instead of `regulated-bank`. Regulated adopters change nothing.

versions.headline: Brownfield assessment — point it at an existing repository
notes: `node assess.mjs --dest <repo>` reports where an existing codebase stands and what adopting would cost, per tier, from a real dry-run install. The last entry point that assumed a greenfield repo.

It separates observed facts from inferences, and prints what it CANNOT see — branch protection, whether CODEOWNERS teams are real reviewers, whether the tests assert anything — on every run. Nothing it prints says a control is operating.
It recommends a starting tier (usually core) and a base profile chosen from the profiles this bundle actually ships, never one you do not have.

versions.headline: The waist gate stops going quiet — nesting fixed, coverage stated, and a backlog example that cannot drift
notes: HG-0007 could be defeated by an entirely ordinary backlog. A milestone keyed by `id` looks exactly like a backlog item, so under the old block boundary it swallowed every item beneath it: the id resolved to the MILESTONE's, that matched no feature pattern, and the gate reported OK over a backlog it had not examined. Milestones keyed by `name` were never affected, which is why it went unseen. Items now end at the next item start at any indent, so both nesting styles and flat files are read the same way.

The gate now has to have examined something before it may print OK, and says how much: `OK (1 of 3 backlog item(s) waist-gated)`. A backlog with content but no recognised item FAILS rather than passing quietly — a mapping-shaped file, or any shape the parser does not understand.

An `ADOPT:` marker still on the shipped `^STORY-\d+$` while no item matches it now FAILS too. Every brownfield repo has ids like FEAT-102 or PAY-88, and until the marker was set the waist of the double diamond read the whole backlog and gated none of it, in green. A marker you DID set that matches nothing today is an ordinary state of a backlog and is only reported.

docs/backlog.example.yaml is installed beside where your backlog goes — both milestone styles, a feature item, an infra item, an exemption, the inline flow form. The test suite parses it and asserts the exact items, so the documented shape cannot drift from the shape the gate understands. That drift is what made the shape ambiguous in the first place: nothing ever shipped an example.
action_required: Set FEATURE in scripts/discovery-link-check.mjs (the 'ADOPT:' line) to your own feature-item id convention. If you left it on the default and your ids look nothing like STORY-<n>, this upgrade turns a false green into a red — the gate was never gating anything.

If your backlog nests items under milestones keyed by `id`, items that were silently skipped will now be examined. Expect findings on pending features with no discovery hand-off: link them, or set 'discovery_exempt: true' with a reason.

versions.headline: The discovery machinery's divergence from ofbo is counted instead of remembered
notes: The discovery tree exists twice — here as the generic harness, and in openfinance-os/ofbo as the instantiation it was extracted from on 2026-07-17. The repository instructions have carried a standing note that the two must be kept in step, with nothing mechanical behind it. The adoption dry-run proves the tree still WORKS; nothing proved it still MATCHES, and nothing counted what was owed.

New `discovery-sync-check` gate over a `discovery-sync.json` ledger: change a file under harness/discovery/ without declaring it and the build fails. Measured on arrival, 7 files had diverged across four workstreams (rc.8 WS8 BrainKit provenance, rc.10 enforcement hardening, WS3 F5 regulated requirements, Phase 1 correctness) and 1 was added here that never existed upstream — 8 of 23 carrying an outstanding port, none of it visible anywhere before now.

The gate is deliberate about what it cannot see. It reads one side, so it NEVER reports the two trees as agreeing, and it prints that limit on every run including a clean one. Only `--upstream <checkout>`, run where both repositories are reachable, performs the three-way comparison and may retire a debt; `--record` may write what this side looks like and nothing about ofbo.

The comparison uses the shared ancestor (the extraction content, which this repository's history can prove) rather than the latest recorded digest. Using the latter inverts the verdict on exactly the files that carry a debt — it reports 'forward-port' for work we hardened, which would overwrite the hardening with the content it replaced. A regression test pins it.

versions.headline: Three authoring skills — release, re-perform, govern
notes: `release` walks delivery ⑦/⑧: re-run the gates at the released commit, assemble and seal the evidence bundle, then STOP. It never authorizes production and never writes activation evidence — it assembles the case a human authorizes.
`re-perform` gives the third line a read-only path: it re-runs a gate independently and writes a re-performance report. It changes nothing — a discrepancy is a finding, not a task.
`govern` guides authoring of a governed artifact behind an ADOPT/mount seam. The agent formats; the accountable human supplies the judgement.

The delivery-harness canon ⑧ was corrected: it listed five evidence items where evidence-seal-check's REQUIRED_TYPES is nine and different. The token-spend ledger seals alongside them but is deliberately not required — cost is telemetry, never a merge input.
action_required: These three, like the other five, are hand-copied: harness/skills/*/SKILL.md → .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md. adopt.mjs does not install them.

release/SKILL.md carries five ADOPT markers — the pre-production promotion command and environment, the smoke command and its URL, the decision-log capture wiring, the eval-rig command, and the production promotion path together with who is entitled to run it.
re-perform/SKILL.md carries one — the audit repository or store the re-performance report is written to. It does not belong on the release branch.

versions.headline: The discovery-sync ledger can actually be reconciled — rc.29 documented a flag it never implemented
notes: `--reconcile` was described in the gate's header, its catalog note and its release notes, and did not exist. Passing it printed the comparison and silently changed nothing, while the operator believed a sync point had been stamped. That is the precise defect class the rc.26 self-claims gate was built for — a claim with no evidence behind it — shipped inside the gate written to prevent it.

It is implemented now, with `--ref <sha>` to record which upstream commit was compared. A stamp records that somebody LOOKED, not that everything agreed: files that match become the new shared base; files that still differ keep their old base and their debt, and gain a real upstream digest.

Three states join the ledger, reachable only by having seen ofbo: `reconciled` (the two agree), `behind` (upstream moved and this side did not — forward-port), `diverged` (both moved, or no shared ancestor — needs a merge). Together with `owed` they say which way each port runs.

rc.29 asserted `last_reconciled === null` outright, in CI and in a test. That reads as strictness and is the opposite: it froze today's state as an invariant, so the first correct reconciliation would have turned the build red with no fix but deleting the check. The rule is now conditional and enforced by checkClaims — an upstream digest or a seen-only state without a recorded reconciliation fails, and a genuine reconciliation passes. CI tests both directions.

versions.headline: The self-claims gate learns the defect class it missed: a documented CLI flag must exist
notes: rc.29 advertised `--reconcile` in a gate's own usage line and never implemented it; rc.31 wrote it. This closes the class rather than the instance. self-claims-check gained C5: a flag a CLI documents about itself must appear in its code.

C1 could not have caught it. C1 checks that a cited script PATH resolves, and the script existed — only its advertised behaviour did not. A tool that accepts a flag and silently does nothing is worse than one that rejects it, because the operator walks away believing it worked.

The rule is narrow on purpose. A flag counts as documented only on a comment line that names its own file — the usage lines these CLIs already carry — so prose about git's `--force-with-lease` or a sibling script's `--tier` is not a claim. Comment-stripping is conservative, so it errs toward missing a defect rather than inventing one: a gate that cries wolf gets switched off, and then it protects nothing.

Measured, not asserted: zero false positives across the 61 flag-documenting scripts, and the rule is pinned against the ACTUAL rc.29 blob from git history rather than a synthetic fixture. A negative bypass test in CI mutates the very file the fault shipped in.

versions.headline: Flow-plan Phase 0 — the found defects, fixed
notes: Capability aggregation across governed changes is strongest-wins (it was first-wins by directory order, which could silently weaken a minimum version/tier).
Gate path scopes match a file exactly or as a directory prefix — docs/backlog.yaml no longer implicates docs/backlog.yaml.bak.
The gate runner refuses a lane with no runnable catalogued controls (exit 2) — an empty lane was a CI step that structurally could not fail.

ci-catalog-check fails two controls sharing one mechanism_ref with different mechanism_args (the runner executed only one variant while reporting both), and prints the execute:false inventory on every run.
evidence-seal-check and release-attestation-check resolve the evidence manifest from one shared list.
A first adopt.mjs run with no --tier lands core, not full.
action_required: If your .github/workflows/ci.yml still invokes `gate-runner --lane build` or `--lane deploy`, remove those lines (or catalogue a control for those lanes): the runner now fails an empty lane instead of passing about nothing. The reference ci.yml shows the new shape.
If you relied on unflagged adopt.mjs runs landing the full tier on a FRESH repo, pass --tier full explicitly (re-runs keep the tier already stamped, as before).

versions.headline: Flow-plan Phase 1 — risk-proportionality made real at execution time
notes: Terminal change states: `closed` and `superseded` end a change. A terminal change stops contributing compiled requirements (the requirement union no longer grows forever), skips plan reconciliation and receipts, and keeps only its classification record.

Per-diff requirement scoping: the gate runner aggregates requirements from the changes THIS diff implicates (the envelope directory, or the envelope's optional `scope_paths` prefixes). No base means every non-terminal change counts, as before. The run record states the scope, the implicated changes, and the max tier.

Tier-aware selection: a catalog control may declare `min_tier` — it runs only when the highest implicated change tier reaches it. `always` and plan-mandated controls override upward. The shipped catalog declares none; this is the adopter knob for a genuinely shorter documentation-PR route.

The reference ci.yml runs the scheduled lane on a cron trigger (plus push-to-main) instead of every PR, and runs the bundle test suite and the two bundle-only gates only where no adoption stamp exists — an adopted repo keeps a compiler/runner/layering smoke instead of the ~1,400-test bundle suite.
`loom gates` runs the pr-lane gate run locally against the merge base — same runner, catalog, and recorded skips as CI; `loom compile` forwards to the policy compiler.
action_required: Close finished changes: set `current_state: closed` (or `superseded`) on governed changes that shipped or were abandoned — until you do, their compiled requirements keep mandating gates on every diff-unknown run.
Optionally declare `scope_paths` on active envelopes so code-only PRs implicate the right change, and `min_tier` on catalog controls you want tier-scoped.
Adopt the new ci.yml shape (the installer drops it as a .loom-new sidecar if you have edited yours): scheduled lane on cron, bundle-only steps stamped out.

versions.headline: Flow-plan Phase 2 (first half) — evidence is derived, not authored
notes: scripts/seal-evidence.mjs (also `loom seal`): the evidence manifest is now DERIVED from the artifacts — it hashes every file in docs/governance/evidence/, orders entries by the seal gate's required-types contract, binds release_commit (git HEAD, or --commit), sets the anchor to the final seal, and re-verifies its own output with the seal gate's evaluate() BEFORE writing. A bundle that would fail verification is never written; files that are not evidence are listed, never silently ignored.

core/gate-runner.mjs --emit-dir <dir>: the runner captures each mechanism's output (still printed verbatim, so logs read the same) and emits one {gate, controls, result, findings_excerpt, commit, produced_at} record per mechanism plus the run record (gate-run.json) — control-plane-style evidence becomes a gate OUTPUT rather than a human transcription. The run record keeps every rc.34 field and gains produced_at.

The gate-run record joins the evidence chain: the seal gate's semantics now verify a sealed gate-run artifact (result must be 'pass'; a named commit must be the release commit). Deliberately NOT added to the required floor — existing bundles keep passing without one; the collector seals it whenever the runner's emitted record is present in the evidence directory.
skills/release/SKILL.md steps 3–4 now run the collector instead of narrating hand-chaining — a hand-typed verdict is exactly the fabricatable evidence the seal was built to refuse.
action_required: Stop hand-building docs/governance/evidence/manifest.json: run `node scripts/seal-evidence.mjs --commit <release-sha>` (or `loom seal`) after copying the release artifacts in. Note it drops a pre-existing manifest attestation loudly — the anchor changes when the chain is rebuilt, so re-anchor and re-attest.
Optionally add --emit-dir to your release-lane gate-runner invocation and copy the emitted gate-run.json into the evidence directory so the run record is sealed with the bundle.

versions.headline: Flow-plan Phase 2 (second half) — signed drills, signed residency, and the deferred D3/D4/D5 closed
notes: ONE attestation stack, the strong one (D3): core/attestations.mjs verifySignatureOver now refuses `demo: true` issuers, honours issuer `valid_from`/`valid_until`/`revoked`, and honours a per-attestation `validity` {issued_at, expires_at, revoked} when present — applied to EVERY signature the harness verifies (evidence anchors, assurance cycles, platform activations, adapter evidence, projections, approval assertions and transcriptions). core/approval-attestations.mjs delegates to it instead of carrying its own copy.
The evidence anchor is MANDATORY (D4): a manifest that omits the `anchor` field no longer skips anchor verification — it fails. Near-free since rc.35: the collector always writes it.

release_commit must be REAL (D5): the seal gate verifies it exists in this repository (`git cat-file -e`) and is an ancestor of HEAD (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`). Outside a git checkout the check is recorded as not-performable — a printed note, never a silent pass. scripts/seal-evidence.mjs refuses to seal against a commit that fails the check.

Drills are SIGNED OBSERVATIONS (Phase 2.4): service-readiness drill fields (bcp_dr.last_exercised, rollback.last_drilled, kill_switch.last_tested, capacity.last_run) take the observation shape proven by platform-activation-example/ — observed_at + observation + a negative_test the mechanism REFUSED + an observer_identity outside the builders group + an ed25519 attestation by a registered issuer over drillHash(record). A bare ISO-date string is accepted for THIS release with a printed deprecation NOTICE.

Residency joins the signed world (Phase 2.5): docs/governance/residency-approval.json (schema loom.residency-approval/v1; {role, registry_id, verdict, decided_at, assertion} per required role) is verified through the approval-attestation core — canonical payload, nonce binding, assertion-issuer registry, service keys refused, demo keys refused. The markdown-table record remains for THIS release as a deprecated fallback with a printed migration notice.

The committed evidence-example is now deliberately refusable (demo anchor + fictional commit); evidence-example/regenerate.mjs re-derives and re-signs it per run with a fresh non-demo key, and the repo CI dry-run does exactly that.
action_required: Replace `demo-anchor-signer` wherever your evidence anchor still relies on it: register your own issuer in docs/governance/attestation-issuers.json and re-sign the anchor (see evidence-example/regenerate.mjs for the per-run pattern). A demo-signed anchor now FAILS release-attestation and change-envelope evidence checks.
Re-seal any manifest that has no `anchor` field: run `node scripts/seal-evidence.mjs --commit <release-sha>` — the collector writes the anchor and self-verifies.
Ensure your evidence manifest's release_commit is the commit you actually released from this repository's history; evidence sealed from a foreign or rewritten commit now fails the seal gate.

Migrate drill records in docs/governance/services/*.json from bare dates to signed observations before the NEXT release — the bare-date form prints a deprecation notice now and is removed in one release.
Migrate the residency record to docs/governance/residency-approval.json before the NEXT release — the markdown parser prints a migration notice now and is removed in one release.

versions.headline: Flow-plan Phase 3 — the value stream is instrumented (and none of it gates)
notes: state_history on the change envelope (Phase 3.1): an append-only [{state, at, by}] record validated by scripts/change-envelope-check.mjs — states advance in the STATES order, `at` never moves backwards, nothing follows a terminal state, `by` resolves in the identity registry when present, and the LAST entry is current_state (so the history cannot become a parallel account of a change that went somewhere else). It is validated in every state, terminal included. One field makes lead time, stage residency, queue age and deployment frequency computable with zero new ceremony.

The state_history requirement is SPLIT, not retroactive: optional wherever it is absent today, REQUIRED at high/critical tiers for changes classified on or after 2026-07-28 (STATE_HISTORY_REQUIRED_FROM). A high-tier change from before the cutover with no history prints a grandfathering NOTICE on every run — never a silent excuse. An unparseable or missing classified_at counts as on-or-after: an unknown input fails toward more control.

scripts/flow-report.mjs (Phase 3.2) — TELEMETRY, NEVER A GATE, in the exact posture of scripts/token-report.mjs. Lead time (classified → in-production), stage-residency histogram, deployment frequency (production transitions plus sealed release records, reported side by side rather than averaged), change-failure rate and MTTR from the operations log, and gate wall-clock per lane from the `ms` the runner has recorded since rc.34 and nothing read. Every figure names its denominator and says when it cannot be computed. `--check` validates INPUT SHAPE only.

Operations signals link to changes (Phase 3.3): two OPTIONAL fields on each entry, validated by scripts/operations-signal-check.mjs — `caused_by_change` (must resolve to a governed change under docs/governance/changes/; where there is no changes tree the attribution is reported NOT VERIFIED rather than passing quietly) and `resolved_at` (must parse, and may not precede `detected`). Without them change-failure rate and MTTR are not derivable at all.

scripts/approval-status.mjs (Phase 3.4) — the approval queue / WIP report, also telemetry. Per change, the roles still owed at PA1 and PA2 with their age, read from the same set scripts/product-approval-check.mjs computes (checkApprovals now RETURNS {findings, missing} instead of discarding the set into finding strings — no second, drifting definition of a required role). The age clock starts when the change entered the state it is sitting in; with no state_history it falls back to classified_at and SAYS the age is approximate. docs/governance/approval-sla.json (new governance/approval-sla.template.json, shaped like assurance-sla) states per-stage and per-role targets and a soft WIP limit; breaches are FLAGGED and gate nothing.

scripts/comprehension-report.mjs (Phase 3.5) — trends `review_minutes` and `pct_agent_generated` per reviewer and over time from the comprehension.json records that have been collected since rc.15 and never read. Fewer than four data points reports `not enough history` rather than a decorated guess. Telemetry; comprehension-check already says these metrics are reported and never gated on their values.

scripts/exception-register-check.mjs (Phase 3.6) — a new catalogued control (EXCEPTION-REGISTER, scheduled lane) projecting EVERY open exception in the repository into one register: envelope exemptions and assurance risk-acceptances alike. Expiry WARNINGS at 30/14/7 days are notices that never fail a build — the hard block stays exactly where it was, at expiry; what is removed is the overnight green-to-blocked surprise. Per-owner and per-control aggregation. CONCENTRATION FAILS: more than 3 open exceptions against one control is one control the organisation has stopped operating, recorded 3+ times. The limit lives in docs/governance/exception-policy.json (new template) and may be TIGHTENED below the shipped floor and never raised above it — a file asking for 10 is itself a finding.

Warning bands elsewhere (Phase 3.6): scripts/operational-readiness-check.mjs and scripts/adoption-attest.mjs print a NOTICE at 80% of each freshness window (WARN_AT). Both still pass; both still block at exactly the same place they always did.

The three reports are wired into ci/ci.yml beside the token report with `--check`, and each is named with its reason in the printed REPORT_ONLY list of scripts/ci-catalog-check.mjs. A merge gated on a duration is a merge gated on the clock; the cheapest way to make that build green is to approve without reading.
action_required: Start appending to `state_history` when a change moves state — {state, at, by}, in transition order. It is optional on your existing envelopes and stays that way; it becomes REQUIRED for high/critical changes you classify from 2026-07-28 onward. `node scripts/change-envelope-check.mjs` prints a NOTICE naming every grandfathered high-tier change so you can see what will never be measurable.

Copy governance/approval-sla.template.json to docs/governance/approval-sla.json and set targets your organisation can actually meet (or omit it — targets fall back to the shipped default of 10 days). Nothing fails when a target is missed.

Copy governance/exception-policy.template.json to docs/governance/exception-policy.json if you want a concentration limit tighter than 3. The scheduled lane now runs the exception register; if you carry more than 3 open exceptions against one control today, that build fails and the register names them.

Add `caused_by_change` and `resolved_at` to operations signals you can attribute and have closed. Both are optional, and change-failure rate / MTTR are only as good as they are — the report says how many signals are unattributed rather than assuming them away.

Optionally add `node scripts/flow-report.mjs`, `node scripts/approval-status.mjs` and `node scripts/comprehension-report.mjs` (without --check) to a scheduled job so the numbers land in a log a human reads. They exit 0 by design.

versions.headline: Flow-plan Phase 4 — approvals re-priced, never removed
notes: Narrowed approval binding: an approval attestation now carries a per-role binding_hash over what that role actually saw (its compiled sections, its role entry, the subject digests) alongside the whole-plan plan_hash. An edit elsewhere in the plan — a comment in an unrelated profile, a new section for another function — no longer invalidates every signature on every in-flight change. Anything within the role’s own scope still invalidates: tamper-evidence is unchanged, only its blast radius is.

Change classes: change_class standard|normal|emergency (default normal). An emergency change compiles the SAME requirements and may reach production through the new emergency-authorized state, but only with a retrospective_deadline; once that deadline passes with receipts still outstanding, the gate fails. Nothing is dropped — it is reordered, with a hard expiry.

Pre-approved change patterns: a profile may carry patterns (pattern_id, matcher, pre-compiled plan hash, second-line approver, expiry, sampling_rate). A standard-class envelope naming a pattern compiles to the pre-approved plan and is enrolled for post-hoc sampling. Patterns expire, a builder may not approve one, and a matcher miss falls back to the full route.

Release trains: docs/governance/release-trains/<id>.json names N change_ids against one sealed bundle. Release-level acts (the hold, the anchor, the freshness) are taken once per train; per-change PA2 is untouched.

Delegation and quorum: an identity may carry delegates [{to, from, until, granted_by}] — a delegate inherits every disjointness rule and the delegation expires. Roles may declare a quorum (any K of the holders) where approvals are checked.

Objections pulled left: the lending and consumer-lending profiles now bind credit-risk and data-protection at PA1 rather than PA2, so those functions see a change at permission-to-develop instead of at permission-to-launch. Pure profile data — the mechanism has existed since 1.11 and was unused.

Flag corroboration: an envelope flag contradicted by the repository’s own governance data is a finding — personal_data:false against a personal category in the data lifecycle, model_involved:false against a non-empty model manifest, third_party:false against a populated third-parties passport section.
action_required: Re-sign nothing: existing approval attestations remain valid. New approvals gain the binding_hash automatically; the whole-plan hash is still recorded.
If you want the emergency lane, decide who may set change_class: emergency and what retrospective_deadline your policy allows — an emergency change with no deadline is refused.
Pattern authors: a pattern is itself a governed change. Add patterns to a profile only with second-line approval, an expiry, and a sampling rate you will actually honour.

Lending adopters: credit-risk and data-protection are now PA1 approvers for lending products. In-flight lending changes past permission-to-develop need those two approvals recorded before their next state transition.

versions.headline: Flow-plan Phase 5 — exposure decoupled from deploy
notes: Environments are a seam, not prose. docs/governance/environments.json (installed from governance/environments.template.json, `governed` tier) declares the promotion ladder: one entry per environment with its purpose, data_classification, url, the identity entitled to promote INTO it, and what it promotes FROM. scripts/environments-check.mjs (ENVIRONMENTS, pr lane) holds five properties — one root and no cycles, a resolvable promoter who is neither an agent nor a builder wherever approval is required, personal data never behind an unattended promotion, and an always-approval-required terminal environment. This replaces the three <!-- ADOPT --> comments in skills/release/SKILL.md that told you to name your pre-production target and could never be checked; the skill now READS the ladder.

Exposure is separated from deploy and governed. docs/governance/feature-flags.json (from governance/feature-flags.template.json, `governed` tier) is the exposure register: every flag defaults OFF, belongs to a governed change, names a human registry owner and a kill path, sits at one of the pilot playbook's six cohort stages, and EXPIRES. scripts/feature-flag-check.mjs (EXPOSURE-CONTROL, pr lane) is MANDATORY-WHEN-COMPILED: silent for a repository doing no staged exposure, and required the moment any compiled plan asks for the new `exposure_control` capability — which profiles/regulated-bank.json now declares at HIGH tier. An expired flag fails (30/14/7-day notices precede it) and a flag whose owning change is closed or superseded fails as stale exposure machinery, so flag debt is visible rather than permanent.

R3b — progressive delivery in service readiness. A service may declare progressive_delivery {strategy: canary|blue-green|ring, stages[{name, traffic_pct, bake_minutes, slo_refs}], automated_rollback{trigger_slo, last_tested}, feature_flag_ref}. The ramp must strictly increase and end at 100, each stage must bake while watching a named SLO, the automated rollback must fire on an SLO the ramp actually observes, and last_tested is a SIGNED OBSERVATION (rc.36's shape) on a 90-day window with the 80% warning band. Optional for a service nobody is ramping; required once a compiled plan asks for exposure_control.

The deploy lane has its first control. scripts/deployed-digest-check.mjs (DEPLOYED-DIGEST, deploy lane) verifies a docs/governance/deployments/<id>.json record against two things nothing else in the harness ever checked: that the deployed digest IS the release subject's authorized artifact digest — a rebuild of the same source is a different artifact and was not the one evaluated — and that the recorded stages replay the declared progressive-delivery ramp in order, at the declared traffic, each having baked at least its declared time. Promotion into an approval-required environment additionally needs an authorized_by who is a non-builder human and not the deployer.

ci/ci.yml runs the deploy lane again, gated on release events (a tag push or a published release). rc.33's empty-lane guard is unchanged and still refuses a lane with no runnable control — what changed is that `deploy` now has one. `build` remains deliberately un-invoked: it still carries zero controls.

Nothing here gates on time, cost or a metric value. The deploy gate reads a clock only to compare the bake a human DECLARED with the bake that was OBSERVED — a control being verified, the same shape as a freshness window, and the opposite of gating a merge on how long something took.
action_required: Recompile every change whose plan compiles at HIGH tier against the regulated-bank profile: it now carries the exposure_control capability, so its plan_hash has moved and change-envelope-check will report the stored plan as stale until you run `node core/policy-compiler.mjs <envelope> --write`. Approval attestations bound to the old plan_hash must be re-collected or re-signed — the bundled worked example shows the shape (approval-attestation-example/regenerate.mjs).

Once a plan compiles exposure_control, THREE things become required and each fails closed until you supply it: docs/governance/feature-flags.json with a flag naming that change; a progressive_delivery block on every service the change declares; and (on the deploy lane) a deployment record binding the deployed digest. If you are not doing staged exposure yet, remove `exposure_control` from your own copy of profiles/regulated-bank.json BEFORE upgrading — the capability is profile data, and this is the one honest way to defer it.

Adopt docs/governance/environments.json. The installed template is the Loom's EXAMPLE ladder and says so: every run prints a NOTICE naming the example.invalid URLs. The gate passes on it, deliberately (a template that fails on install gets deleted), but a deployment record can only cite an environment you have actually declared.

If your CI copies ci/ci.yml, note the new `on:` triggers (tag pushes matching v*, and published releases) and adjust the tag pattern to yours. Where your platform deploys from a workflow_dispatch or a deployment event, widen the deploy step's `if:` — the rule is that the step runs wherever a docs/governance/deployments/ record is written.

CODEOWNERS needs no edit: environments.json, feature-flags.json and deployments/ all sit under /docs/governance/, which the shipped template already owns. scripts/control-plane-check.mjs now probes all three plus the two new gate scripts, so a repository that has narrowed that rule will hear about it.

versions.headline: Flow-plan Phase 6 — the machinery runs in parallel, and says so
notes: core/gate-runner.mjs executes a BOUNDED-CONCURRENCY POOL instead of a serial spawnSync loop. `--jobs N` (default availableParallelism()-1, floor 1) sizes it; `--timeout-ms N` (default 300000) bounds each gate — a hung gate used to hang CI forever, and is now KILLED and recorded with status `timeout`, which counts as a failure and never as a pass or a skip. Output is captured per gate (rc.35's capture, unchanged) and FLUSHED IN CATALOG ORDER once the pool drains, so a parallel run's log reads exactly like the serial one's. Every rc.34/rc.35 record field survives; `concurrency: {jobs, timeout_ms, waves}` and a `wave` per execution are added.

Catalog entries may declare `depends_on: [control_id]`, and the runner turns the graph into topological waves. Real ids only, no self-reference, and cycles are refused by BOTH scripts/control-catalog-check.mjs (catalog-wide) and the runner (exit 2) — a cycle is never flattened, because then the declared order would not be the executed order. A dependency on a control THIS run skipped is not a barrier: it was skipped, with its reason already recorded. The shipped catalog declares the two real dependencies: RELEASE-ATTESTATION after RELEASE-SUBJECT + HG-0003, and FLOOR-DRIFT after FREEZE-STAMP.

core/gate-cache.mjs (GATE-CACHE, pr lane, execute:false) is a content-addressed result cache under .loom/gate-cache/. The key covers the mechanism FILE's digest, its arguments, the canonical catalog entry of every control sharing it, the digest of every file under the control's DECLARED PATH SCOPE, the sorted compiled plan_hash set, and a format version. Four rules keep a hit honest: only controls that DECLARE a path scope are cacheable (that scope is already what decides whether the control runs at all on a diff, so the cache adds no new trust); `always:true` tamper checks and unscoped controls never are; the RELEASE and DEPLOY lanes never are, whatever a control declares; and only PASSES are stored, so a failure always re-runs. A hit is recorded as status `pass-cached` with its `cache_key`, and the stored output is replayed verbatim — as auditable as a skip. `--no-cache` disables it, and the record says which it was.
core/compiled-requirements.mjs now carries each counted change's `plan_hash` on its aggregate entry — that is what makes recompiling any plan invalidate every cached result in the run.
ci/ci.yml caches .loom/gate-cache with actions/cache, under a comment stating the trust argument in full. Losing the cache costs time and nothing else: a miss runs the gate.

skills/next-story and skills/discovery dispatch their reviewers in ONE message, so they run concurrently and blind to each other — the wording already proven in skills/develop. A reviewer that has read the other's verdict was never a second pair of eyes, so this is a wall-clock cut with no control cost.

skills/next-story gains a documented `--parallel N` lane (§6): up to N pending items that are mutually DAG-independent via depends_on AND disjoint in a new optional `paths:` field on backlog items, each in its own git worktree, branch and PR. An item with NO `paths:` may only run alone — an undeclared scope is not an empty one. Plus a stacked-PR subsection (`stacked_on: <PR#>`) so a dependent story's REVIEW can start while merge order stays human-controlled and follows the stack. Documentation and the backlog example's schema; no new script, and four-eyes is untouched.

Measured on a staged full-tier adoption (4 cores, 34 mechanisms selected, 2 waves, 21 of them cacheable): serial baseline ~2.35s, cold pooled ~0.98s, warm ~0.45s. Nothing here gates on time, cost or a metric value, and no fail-closed default moved. The timeout is the one new way to fail, and it fails CLOSED: no result inside the bound is a failure, not a pass.
action_required: Add `.loom/gate-cache/` to your .gitignore, or rely on the one the store writes for itself (the runner drops a `*` .gitignore inside the cache directory the first time it stores an entry). A cached result is a local/CI artifact; the record of record remains gate-run-*.json.

If your CI copies ci/ci.yml, take the new `Gate result cache` step (actions/cache@v4 on .loom/gate-cache) or drop it — the runner works either way, a cold cache simply misses. Do NOT extend the cache to the release or deploy lanes: the runner refuses to serve them, and it is the release re-running its gates for real that the refusal protects.

Gate wall-clock in gate-run-*.json is now the CONCURRENT elapsed time per mechanism, so the lane total scripts/flow-report.mjs prints is a sum of overlapping intervals and is no longer the lane's wall-clock. Read `concurrency.waves` and `concurrency.jobs` alongside it.
A gate of yours that takes longer than 300s now fails as a timeout. Raise `--timeout-ms` for that lane deliberately, in the workflow, where the number is reviewable — do not remove the bound.
If you add `depends_on` to your own catalog entries, keep the graph acyclic: control-catalog-check fails the build on a cycle and the runner exits 2 rather than running one.

Adopting the `--parallel` lane is opt-in and needs `paths:` on the backlog items you intend to run together. Until you declare them, every item is treated as touching everything and the lane degrades to one story at a time — which is the current behaviour, and the safe one.

versions.headline: The cache-key module is text again — a control-plane source file that no diff could show
notes: core/gate-cache.mjs shipped at rc.40 with LITERAL NUL, 0x01 and 0x02 bytes embedded in the cache-key template literals as field delimiters. They work at runtime, but they made git and ripgrep classify the file as BINARY: `git show` rendered rc.40 as `Bin 0 -> 7746 bytes`, and a directory-wide `rg` sweep skipped the file silently while still matching it when named explicitly. The module that decides which gates may be served from cache — that is, which gates may not run — was invisible to both review and search. Replaced with the \x00 / \x01 / \x02 ESCAPE SEQUENCES.

The runtime strings are byte-identical, so this is not a cache format change: the pre-change and post-change modules compute the SAME key for the same input (asserted directly, old module vs new module, against a stable mechanism). No stored entry is invalidated and no gate re-runs that would not have. FORMAT is unchanged.
The file is now 145 lines of text to git and is returned by directory-wide greps. Nothing else moved: no gate, catalog entry, profile, template or default changed at this version.
action_required: None. If you vendored core/gate-cache.mjs, re-copy it — your cache stays valid either way, because the key is unchanged.
If you carry your own binary-file policy for source trees, note that this class is worth a check: a .mjs that git reports as Bin is a file your review process cannot show a reviewer.

versions.headline: The waist-gate exemption must state a reason — a silent bypass no longer passes
notes: discovery_exempt: true let a pending feature reach delivery with no justification recorded at all. The header comment, the failure message and the shipped example every one promised a reason was required ("Silence is not an option; an exemption is") — and nothing checked. One line bypassed the gate that makes discovery non-optional, and the gate printed OK.

An exemption now needs a `reason:` a human can argue with. Empty, whitespace-only, and leftover placeholders (TODO / TBD / ADOPT / N/A / <...>) are refused: a placeholder is the same silence dressed as compliance.
Found by testing the gate rather than reading it. The gate had never been asked to refuse anything — it had only ever been run against a backlog with nothing in it.
action_required: BREAKING for any backlog carrying `discovery_exempt: true` without a `reason:`. The build will now fail. Add the reason — that is the fix, and writing it is the control. Do not remove the exemption to dodge the gate; an exemption with a stated reason is a legitimate, auditable choice.

versions.headline: The attestation tests stop failing a repository for assembling its own evidence bundle
notes: core/attestations.test.mjs resolved the evidence manifest in either layout — the bundle example or an adopted repo — and skipped only when NEITHER existed. It then verified the SHIPPED EXAMPLE's ed25519 attestation against whatever it found.

An adopter who follows the adoption guide (adapt evidence-example/ into docs/governance/evidence/) and then assembles a real bundle from their own release has a manifest at that path with a different anchor and, until they sign it, no attestation at all. The suite pointed at that bundle and failed: one assertion failure and two TypeErrors on MANIFEST.attestation.signature. The repository was punished for doing exactly what it was told.

The tests now run when the resolved manifest carries an attestation and skip when it does not. A mounted copy of the example still runs them; an adopter's own unsigned bundle is not this suite's business.
Found by assembling a real evidence bundle in an adopted repo — the release path had never been exercised.
action_required: None. If your own bundle was failing these three tests, it will now skip them. Sign your anchor and they run again.

versions.headline: Shari'ah governance becomes a plane of the harness — and stays dormant for every repository that does not compile it
notes: Ten new catalogued controls. Six are MECHANICALLY-VALIDATED with a gate and a suite behind them — SHARIAH-GOV (scripts/shariah-governance-check.mjs), SHARIAH-SUBSTANCE (shariah-emission-check.mjs), PURIFICATION (purification-check.mjs), PROFIT-DISTRIBUTION (profit-distribution-check.mjs), KNOWLEDGE-CURRENCY (knowledge-staleness-check.mjs) and EVIDENCE-RETENTION (evidence-retention-check.mjs), all on the pr lane. HOOK-SHARIAH-TERM is the new pre-write guard. AI-INCIDENT is DEFINED and no more than that: it is a runbook (docs/governance/runbooks/ai-incident-runbook.md), not a mechanism. AI-FAIRNESS and AI-EXPLAINABILITY are catalogued ABSENT — declared gaps with nothing behind them, written down because an uncatalogued gap is the one nobody argues about.

Every one of the six is MANDATORY-WHEN-COMPILED, the rc.39 exposure_control posture: inert for a repository whose compiled plans never ask for the capability, and required — fail-closed, from the first run — the moment one does. Nothing here is switched on by a CI flag, an environment variable or the mere presence of a file; the requirement arrives from a profile or it does not arrive. On a fresh full-tier adoption all six run and pass on the shipped state, three of them printing nothing at all. NO ISLAMIC CONTROL FAILS A CONVENTIONAL REPOSITORY — but do not read that as 'this wave changes nothing for you', because it is not true of the wave: the same wave tightened two SHIPPED profiles, and a conventional repository can meet a new hard failure it never opted into. Both are in the action list, with their remedies.

The capability names a profile may now require: `shariah_governance`, `knowledge_currency` (products/islamic-product and the institution template), `shariah_model_validation` (products/shariah-model — a DOMAIN validation stacked on top of model_risk, never instead of it), `runtime_guardrails` (products/ai-decision-system at high), `real_data_controls` (regulated-bank at high) and `evidence_retention` (no shipped profile declares it; an institution declares it in its own).

FIVE SHIPPED PROFILES CHANGED CONTENT, and two of those changes bite a CONVENTIONAL repository. profiles/regulated-bank.json adds `real_data_controls` at HIGH; profiles/products/ai-decision-system.json adds `runtime_guardrails` at HIGH plus an `ai-disclosure` PA2 section at medium — neither is conditional on the `islamic` flag and both are new hard failures. The other three are inert where they were inert before: products/islamic-product carries the role rename, products/open-finance gains an islamic-ONLY conditional (a conventional Open Finance compile is unchanged), and jurisdictions/uae-bank gains an `open_finance` conditional adding one market-specific customer-experience PA2 section (inert unless an envelope sets the `open_finance` flag AND names that jurisdiction). profiles/standard.json, products/lending, products/consumer-lending, products/payments and the worked institution profile are byte-unchanged. What the tier does NOT protect you from: a profile binding digests the WHOLE profile, so a stored plan naming any of the five is stale at EVERY tier — including tiers where none of its own requirements moved.

BREAKING VOCABULARY: the role `shariah-board` is retired — it appears in no profile, role set, registry or approver list, only in the tests that pin its absence. Three roles replace it because they are three lines, not three names for one body — `shariah-committee` is the internal Shari'ah supervision committee that RULES (a body, with a quorum, declared once in the identity registry), `shariah-compliance` is the second-line function that MONITORS continuously, and `shariah-audit` is third-line internal audit that CERTIFIES what was built and may never be outsourced. A profile still saying `shariah-board` compiles a role nobody holds, and every approval against it is unsatisfiable.

The three roles joined SECOND_LINE_ROLES in scripts/product-approval-check.mjs, so the existing builder-disjointness rule now reaches them: an approver in the `builders` group can no longer issue a Shari'ah approval. This is a TIGHTENING and it is the point — the person who certifies a change may never be an author of it, and a Shari'ah signer sitting in the builders group was previously invisible to that rule.

hooks/pii-guard.sh reads its shapes from pii-patterns.json beside it — mounted DATA, so a new jurisdiction is a row in a file rather than a hand-edit of a security-critical shell script. It fails CLOSED: missing, unparseable, empty, or carrying a malformed row, the guard DENIES the write. A skipped row is indistinguishable from a shape nobody ever added, which is why it refuses rather than continues. The pattern path is resolved beside the script and deliberately not from an environment variable — an overridable path is a disarm switch.

hooks/shariah-term-guard.sh (registered in hooks/settings.hooks.json) is scoped by .claude/hooks/shariah-surfaces.txt and that file SHIPS EMPTY. With no declared surface the guard is a no-op, which is the correct and permanent state for an adopter running no Islamic product.

Six new templates: docs/governance/shariah-rulings.json (the SR-* decision register), issc-register.json, profit-distribution.json, knowledge-pins.json and shariah-audit-charter.md at the `full` tier, evidence-retention.json at `governed` because twelve of its fourteen types are the ordinary release bundle. governance/identities.template.json gained five ISSC seats, the two Shari'ah desks and a `quorum` block; assurance-sla.template.json gained the `shariah-compliance-monitoring` source and the `quarantine-income` / `suspend-product-offering` containments, both of which park VALUE rather than code and both of which a conventional mis-priced fee reaches for too.

Existing gates were extended rather than duplicated: evidence-seal-check gained a tenth evidence type (`shariah-attestation`, plan-only on the brainkit-provenance terms); model-provenance-check gained the domain validations; change-envelope-check reads institution `asserts_flags` and `required_for_all_changes`; operations-signal-check gained the shariah-non-compliance type with its purification and issc-escalation routes; assurance-cycle-check gained named streams; comprehension-check gained deterministic medium-tier sampling; product-approval-check gained the conforming-change lane; control-plane-check probes two more targets. Every extension is inert where its input is absent.

WHAT NONE OF THIS DOES: no gate in this bundle rules on a Shari'ah question, and no agent approves anything. Scholars decide Shari'ah. The harness checks that a cited ruling exists, that an approver held the seat on the day they signed, that a quorum was met, that a purification record names a non-agent human and cites a method that exists on disk — shape, provenance and binding. A green run means the record is well-formed and bound, never that the structure is permissible.
action_required: ACTION REQUIRED, CONVENTIONAL REGULATED ADOPTERS — a NEW hard failure at the HIGH tier, and nothing about it is Islamic. profiles/regulated-bank.json now requires `real_data_controls` at high, so ANY change compiling at high against regulated-bank — Islamic or not, model or not, personal data or not — now fails the provider-selection gate with `PS-R06: a compiled plan requires capability "real_data_controls" but no provider is selected for role "real-data-controls"`. It is a deliberate tightening: the harness is synthetic-only by design and that posture was inherited by SILENCE — a repository that starts carrying real customer data does not announce it, and REAL-PII-SURFACE stays graded `absent` while becoming the surface that matters most. THE REMEDY IS TWO STEPS, NOT ONE: record the decision in docs/governance/provider-selection.json for role `real-data-controls` (shipped providers: `kms-field-encryption`, `vault-tokenisation`), AND copy that provider's file from adapters/providers/real-data-controls/ into docs/governance/adapters/ — a selection with no mounted adapter fails PS-R05 instead, because selecting is not installing. The gate then passes with a `selected, not active` NOTICE until the adapter's activation_evidence carries a real fetch and a passed negative probe. IF YOU ARE GENUINELY SYNTHETIC-ONLY and this is not the release to decide it, remove `real_data_controls` from your own copy of profiles/regulated-bank.json BEFORE upgrading — the capability is profile data, and that is the one honest way to defer it (the same escape rc.39 gave exposure_control). Naming a provider does not mean the harness verified anything operates; it refuses to let a change ship that never named a control.

ACTION REQUIRED, AI-DECISION ADOPTERS — the same shape, a different profile, also not Islamic. profiles/products/ai-decision-system.json now requires `runtime_guardrails` at the HIGH tier, so a high-tier change naming it fails with `PS-R06: a compiled plan requires capability "runtime_guardrails" but no provider is selected for role "runtime-guardrails"`. It exists because every guardrail this bundle ships is a BUILD-time one — hooks and CI gates do not execute in the serving path — so a model deciding about people in production had no recorded enforcement point at all. Same two-step remedy: a selection for role `runtime-guardrails` in docs/governance/provider-selection.json (shipped providers: `gateway-policy-enforcement`, `sidecar-policy-enforcement`) plus that provider's adapter mounted at docs/governance/adapters/. Same honest deferral: remove `runtime_guardrails` from your own copy of the profile. And the same limit, stated rather than implied — the harness cannot verify a runtime guardrail FIRES; it can refuse a change that never chose one, and read the denial the platform recorded for the negative probe. Note also the medium-tier `ai-disclosure` PA2 section this profile gained: regenerate the approval surface, or the section is required and missing.

ACTION REQUIRED, CONVENTIONAL REGULATED ADOPTERS (2 of 2) — profiles/regulated-bank.json also now requires `evidence_retention` at the HIGH tier, so a high-tier change compiling that profile needs docs/governance/evidence-retention.json. The installer mounts the template at the `governed` tier; if you adopted at `core`, take it with `--tier governed` or write the file. It is required rather than optional because a capability no shipped profile can require is a control nothing can ever arm — the gate would be catalogued as mechanically-validated while being unreachable in practice, which is precisely the decorative-control defect this release exists to remove. State a retention period per evidence type; the harness reads the policy and says plainly that it cannot verify any archive actually retains anything.

BREAKING — RECOMPILE, and NOT only if you compile the Islamic profile. FIVE shipped profiles changed content this wave — regulated-bank, products/ai-decision-system, products/islamic-product, products/open-finance, jurisdictions/uae-bank — and a plan binds the WHOLE content of every profile it compiled from. So EVERY stored control plan naming any of the five no longer reconciles with a fresh compile: at EVERY tier, conventional or Islamic, whether or not that tier's own requirements moved. scripts/change-envelope-check.mjs reports them as STALE. THAT IS THE RECONCILIATION MECHANISM WORKING, NOT A FAULT — binding a plan to profile CONTENT is precisely what stops a profile edit riding an old plan unnoticed, and a wave that edits profiles is meant to produce this report. Run `node core/policy-compiler.mjs <envelope> --write` (or `loom compile`) for each affected envelope, regenerate any approval surface (ai-decision-system adds `ai-disclosure` at medium; jurisdictions/uae-bank adds a customer-experience section for open_finance changes), then re-collect or re-sign approval attestations bound to the old plan_hash. Plans naming ONLY profiles/standard, products/lending, products/consumer-lending or products/payments are unaffected. Islamic adopters additionally: `shariah-board` is gone from the compiled role set — replace it in any profile of your own with the role that actually decides the thing you meant.

TIGHTENING, intentional. If a Shari'ah signer of yours is in the `builders` group, product-approval-check will start failing that approval. Move the identity out of `builders` — do not widen the rule. An institution too small to separate them has found the finding the rule exists to surface, and the answer is an exception with a stated owner and an expiry, never a quieter gate.

FAIL-CLOSED: ensure `.claude/hooks/pii-patterns.json` is present and parseable beside pii-guard.sh. The installer mounts it at the core tier and it is not tierable, but if you have CUSTOMISED the hook your edited copy is preserved (the stamp knows it is yours) and the new upstream one lands beside it as `pii-guard.sh.loom-new` — take the pattern loading with you when you merge, or your hook keeps its hardcoded shapes and every jurisdiction stays a shell edit. If the patterns file is ever missing, the guard denies every write rather than passing them unscanned.

Merge the new hook registration: hooks/settings.hooks.json adds shariah-term-guard.sh to PreToolUse and arrives as a `.loom.json` sidecar beside your `.claude/settings.json`. Safe to take even if you run no Islamic product — the guard is a no-op while `.claude/hooks/shariah-surfaces.txt` is empty, which is how it ships.

NEW ADOPT MARKERS at the `full` tier: shariah-rulings.json, issc-register.json, profit-distribution.json, knowledge-pins.json and shariah-audit-charter.md, plus evidence-retention.json at `governed`. `loom configure` lists them. Fill them only if you run an Islamic book — and if you do not, DELETE the ISSC seats and the `quorum` block from your identities.json rather than leaving them as placeholders: a quorum for a role nobody holds is unsatisfiable and blocks every change that would need it.

Islamic adopters only: profiles/institutions/institution.template.json and profiles/jurisdictions/jurisdiction.template.json are new starting points, and a WHOLLY Islamic institution should set `asserts_flags: { "islamic": true }` so no envelope can route around Shari'ah governance by leaving a box unticked. Do NOT assert it if you run both books — there the flag is a real per-change fact and the assertion would be a lie the gate then enforces.

Everyone else: NOT nothing — here is the exact boundary instead of a reassurance. What is true: no Islamic control can fail a conventional repository, no Islamic file is required of you, and on a full-tier adoption the six run and pass on the shipped state. What is NOT true, and was claimed here before this correction was written: that the wave leaves a conventional run unchanged. Three things reach you whatever book you run — the two profile tightenings above at the HIGH tier, the recompile of every stored plan naming one of the five changed profiles, and `.claude/hooks/pii-patterns.json`, which is fail-closed from the first run and is a new file the guard requires. If a control fails on your repository after this upgrade, read the finding before the profile: it names the capability and the role, and the profile that compiled it is where the decision was made.

versions.headline: 2.0.0 — the last two catalogued gaps get mechanisms, and the release candidate ends
notes: AI-FAIRNESS and AI-EXPLAINABILITY were the two controls the catalog carried as ABSENT: named, graded honestly, and backed by nothing. Both are now MECHANICALLY-VALIDATED, and only that. Read the state literally — it is the grade that says a mechanism exists, not that a risk is controlled.

AI-FAIRNESS is scripts/fairness-evaluation-check.mjs over a new docs/governance/fairness-evaluations.json: a protected-attribute register where each attribute carries a legal basis, one disparity metric for the file, a threshold with an EXPLICIT direction, an owner who resolves to a human outside `builders`, and a measurement per registered attribute with an identified population and a re-hashed report artifact. THE HARNESS MEASURES NO DISPARITY. It has no metric, no rig and no population; every number is the adopter's, read as a declaration. A rig measuring the wrong thing produces a record this gate passes.

The rule that made the grade change defensible is FR-R08, the pin binding: an evaluation names the model_id and prompt_version it was run against, and the gate compares them to the model manifest. A retrain that moves the pin therefore invalidates its own fairness evidence. That is the mechanical half of 're-tested on every material retrain', and it is the one property a filled-in eval slot could never hold — which is exactly why rc.46 refused to grade this control on the strength of the slot.

FR-R04 makes threshold DIRECTION explicit rather than inferred. A difference metric fails high; a ratio metric where 1.0 is parity fails LOW. Inferring that from the metric string is how a failing model reads green, so the field is declared and a wrong direction is a finding, not a guess.

AI-EXPLAINABILITY is scripts/decision-contestability-check.mjs over a new docs/governance/decision-contestability.json. The `explainability-and-contestability` PA2 section has always existed and has always been prose an approver reads; the hole was that it joined to nothing, so A PLAN COULD SATISFY IT WHILE A MODEL SHIPPED THAT THE PROSE NEVER MENTIONED. CT-R02 is that join: a covered-tier role in the model manifest with no declared contest route is named.

Around it: where the reason actually appears (a reason that exists only in a log is not a reason anybody was given), what the shown reason is DERIVED from, a bounded response time, an authority who resolves to a human who is neither an agent nor a builder, and somewhere overturns are recorded so the runtime monitoring can see them. CT-R11 reports the standing limit on EVERY run for every surface: nothing here generates a reason, judges whether one is intelligible to the person who received it, delivers anything to a customer, or routes a contest.

Both are MANDATORY-WHEN-COMPILED on new capabilities (`fairness_evaluation`, `decision_contestability`), the rc.39 exposure_control posture with rc.46's correction: arming on a file's PRESENCE is a defect, because the installer mounts templates into repositories that never asked for them. A repository whose compiled plans never require the capability is INERT and both gates report so; the moment one does, the same rules are findings that name the change id.

Both templates install at the GOVERNED tier, alongside product-evals.json. Their join partners — model-manifest.json and identities.json — are core, so nothing about the join depends on tier. A core-tier adoption that compiles either capability is told in the failure message which template it needs and that raising the tier is how it arrives, rather than being handed a filename the bundle did not install at its tier.
AI-INCIDENT is unchanged and remains DEFINED: a runbook, not a mechanism. Nothing in this release watches a live model, evaluates a production output, pages a human or moves money.

The version is 2.0.0. Forty-six release candidates end here, and the number carries no claim beyond the catalog: 2.0.0 is the point at which every control the catalog names has either a mechanism behind it or a note saying plainly that it does not.

PILOT-CONDUCT is new and MECHANICALLY-VALIDATED (scripts/pilot-record-check.mjs, docs/governance/pilot-record.json). SUPERVISED-PILOT beside it stays ABSENT, and that is the point: the pilot is an EVENT, and grading it on the strength of the instrument would be the exact substitution the catalog's grammar exists to prevent. A green gate over an empty pilot is still an empty pilot.

The rule that earns the new grade is PL-R08, a join rather than a field check: the gate parses the adversarial table in runbooks/pilot-playbook.md itself and requires an exercise for every AX row whose status carries `live`. The playbook's own exit criterion — 'every live row exercised at least once and its evidence retained' — was until now tracked in NO FILE AT ALL. Adding a row to the playbook creates an obligation on the running pilot the moment it is written. Same discipline as discovery-sync.json: a debt nobody wrote down is a debt nobody pays.

The adversarial checklist gained stable AX-nn ids so the record can cite a row without matching its prose. Rewording a row no longer invalidates the record; changing an id or deleting an exercised row is a deliberate act the gate reports.

Around the join: stage monotonicity (no sitting at stage 4 having exited only stage 1), numeric exposure caps, no financial execution before stage 4, a rollback drilled before production exposure, an observer and accountable executive who resolve to humans outside `builders`, risk acceptance reserved to the executive alone, and an independent report whose author is not a builder. While the pilot is `active` outstanding live rows are a NOTICE — a pilot in flight is supposed to have them.

PILOT-CONDUCT arms on CONTENT, not presence and not a compiled capability: a pilot is not a property of any change's control plan, so nothing can compile it. `status: active` is the declaration; until it is set the gate is inert and mounting the template cannot fail anybody.
action_required: ACTION REQUIRED, ADOPTERS OF THE ai-decision-system PROFILE — a NEW hard failure, arriving without a code change on your side. That profile now compiles `fairness_evaluation` and `decision_contestability` from the MEDIUM tier, so the first medium-or-higher change against a model that decides about people fails until two records exist and are filled: docs/governance/fairness-evaluations.json and docs/governance/decision-contestability.json.

Below the governed tier neither template is installed. The failure message names the template and says that raising the tier is how it arrives — an adopter is never handed a filename the bundle did not install at their tier.

NOTHING CHANGES FOR ANY OTHER ADOPTER. Both capabilities compile from that one profile; a repository that does not select it never arms either gate. Mounting the templates cannot fail anybody — every rule is a NOTICE until a compiled plan requires the capability. Verified by an A/B against the previous release rather than asserted.

EXPECT THE MEASUREMENTS TO BE THE SLOW PART. The register is a morning's work; a disparity measured on a population you can defend is not. FR-R08 binds each measurement to the model and prompt pin, so it has to be re-measured whenever either moves — plan that into your retrain path rather than discovering it at the gate.

READ WHAT THE GREEN MEANS. Both gates read records. Neither measures a disparity, judges an explanation, nor routes a contest. A green run says the record exists, is bound to the pin that ships, and names people who resolve — never that the model is fair, and never that a customer can actually contest anything.

NO ACTION for anyone not running a pilot. docs/governance/pilot-record.json installs at core and is INERT until you set `status` to `active` — an untouched copy is silent forever, and no compiled plan can arm it.

IF YOU ARE ABOUT TO PILOT: fill the record before stage 2, not after. Two rules bite retroactively and cannot be satisfied backwards — stage exits need a date, evidence and an approver from outside the build team for every stage you have already left, and a rollback drill must predate production exposure. A pilot that reaches stage 4 and then writes its record will find it cannot honestly produce either.
